extractedText: Everything you want to know about ONDC ONDC - The Revolution Reshaping Indian Ecommerce (Part I) Report this article Kriti Aggarwal Kriti Aggarwal Published Jul 24, 2023 + Follow The Indian ecommerce markets have been growing steadily over the last decade and have crossed new milestones year after year. While the market is expected to cross $100 billion in 2024, the exponential growth has primarily been the hegemony of established giants and big brands, leaving SMBs more or less untouched by this growth. While the likes of Amazon, Flipkart, and Myntra have been making a kill, small and medium-sized offline businesses, and retailers have been marred by dwindling footfalls. COVID-induced disruptions also gravitated buyers towards omnichannel buying, especially via mobile channels. This new trend was further alienating SMBs from mainstream ecommerce until ONDC happened. What is ONDC ( Open Network for Digital Commerce)? ONDC is a Government of India-backed initiative to democratize ecommerce and bring SMBs to mainstream ecommerce. Touted as the UPI for ecommerce, ONDC is going to be a game-changer. After ensuring digital identification and authentication on a population scale with AADHAR and making digital payments seamless with UPI, ONDC is the next step towards the digitization of the huge Indian markets. With its transformative vision and inclusive framework, ONDC is unlocking boundless potential, revolutionizing how businesses operate, and paving the way for a thriving digital commerce space for all participants. Here is what ONDC promises to offer businesses of every scale and size: A unified and transparent digital commerce framework that empowers all participants, especially SMEs, and encourages fair competition Pan-India reach with a focus on hyperlocal commerce Eliminate intermediaries and open up new market opportunities by enabling sellers to connect directly with consumers Trustworthy, transparent transactions using standardized protocols and data exchange mechanisms Superlative tech and fulfillment solutions that offer cost-efficient set-up to streamline business and reduce costs Complete control over the business with the freedom to use one’s own business rules, prices, return/refund policies, etc. Access to customer data to understand and plan for strategic growth Collaborative ecosystem which includes government bodies, technology providers, and other network participants and helps with the ecommerce supply chain Regulatory compliance right from the start to ensure standardized functioning and minimized grievances With these promises and goals in place, ONDC sets the track for India to become a global economic powerhouse. The open network also empowers SMEs and paves the way for disruptive growth. How ONDC will work? Unlike the platform-centric e commerce models, ONDC takes the network approach wherein once registered on the open network sellers and their products will be discoverable by all the customers irrespective of whichever buyer interface customers are using. This is a major departure from how ecommerce was done until now. For example, if a fashion products seller is registered on Amazon, his products were not available on Flipkart, Myntra, or any other marketplace. To be discoverable on each of the platforms sellers had to create separate accounts on each of these platforms. Similarly, if the buyer had to buy fashion products, they had to check on various marketplaces to find the best prices and products. Now both the sellers and the buyers just need one app to sell and find products available on ONDC. What’s even more interesting is that there are a number of seller-facing interfaces, i.e., the tech solutions which sellers can use to list, display, sell and fulfill their products on ONDC. The sellers can pick and choose the best ONDC Seller App as per their requirements. Similarly, buyers can choose from a number of ONDC buyer apps to search for and buy the products they need. How do a typical product search, order, and fulfillment happen on ONDC? To explain the process of product search, order placement, and fulfillment let us take the example of a customer named Ravi, who is planning to buy a formal white colored shirt. Here is a breakdown of his journey on the Open Network For Digital Commerce: Product Search Ravi uses one among the many ONDC buyer apps like say Mystore Buyer App to access all the fashion sellers registered on the ONDC platform. He can start his product search either through a website or mobile application.
